Plot the SROC curves

plot.sroc.Rd

Plot method for objects of class "sroc" returned by reitsma.sroc (one SROC curve) and hattori.tsroc (one time-dependent SROC curve for each time point). For the output of hattori.tsroc, the curves of the time points are drawn one per page by default; in an interactive session the user is prompted ("Hit <Return> to see next plot") before each new page. Alternatively, all the time points can be overlaid in one panel (overlay = TRUE).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sroc'
plot(
  x,
  time = NULL,
  time.index = FALSE,
  overlay = FALSE,
  ask = NULL,
  add.spoint = TRUE,
  spoint.region = FALSE,
  plot.ci = FALSE,
  ci.level = 0.95,
  add.study = FALSE,
  study.size = c("fixed", "precision"),
  study.pch = 1,
  study.cex = 1,
  study.col = NULL,
  add.sauc = TRUE,
  legend.pos = "bottomright",
  sroc.cols = NULL,
  sroc.lty = 1,
  sroc.lwd = 2,
  ci.lty = 2,
  ci.lwd = 1,
  sp.pch = 19,
  sp.cex = 1.2,
  xlab = "FPR (1 - specificity)",
  ylab = "TPR (sensitivity)",
  main = NULL,
  addon = FALSE,
  n.grid = 300,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object of class "sroc" from reitsma.sroc or hattori.tsroc.

time

Time points to plot (only for hattori.tsroc results). Either numeric values of the time points (e.g., c(24, 60)) or integer indices when time.index = TRUE. Default NULL plots all the time points.

time.index

Logical; if TRUE, time is interpreted as the positions of the time points.

overlay

Logical; if TRUE, all the selected time points are drawn in one panel.

ask

Logical; whether to wait for <Return> before each new page. Default NULL means TRUE when more than one page is drawn on an interactive device.

add.spoint

Logical; whether to add the summary operating point.

spoint.region

Logical; whether to add the confidence region of the summary point (an ellipse on the logit scale, back-transformed).

plot.ci

Logical; whether to add pointwise confidence bands of the SROC curve (delta method using var.ml).

ci.level

Confidence level of the bands and the region. Default 0.95.

add.study

Logical; whether to add the observed studies (\((1 - \mathrm{spec}_i, \mathrm{sens}_i)\), after continuity correction) stored in the data element of the fit.

study.size

Size of the study points: "fixed" (default) or "precision", proportional to \(1/\sqrt{v_1 + v_2}\) relative to its mean.

study.pch, study.cex

Symbol and (base) size of the study points.

study.col

Color of the study points. Default NULL uses the curve color, semi-transparent.

add.sauc

Logical; whether to show the SAUC (and its CI) in a legend.

legend.pos

Position of the legend (see legend).

sroc.cols

Color(s) of the SROC curves. Recycled over time points when overlay = TRUE.

sroc.lty, sroc.lwd

Line type and width of the SROC curves.

ci.lty, ci.lwd

Line type and width of the confidence bands.

sp.pch, sp.cex

Symbol and size of the summary points.

xlab, ylab

Axis labels.

main

Main title. Default NULL gives an automatic title (with the time point).

addon

Logical; if TRUE, add to the current plot instead of starting a new one (only when one panel is drawn).

n.grid

Number of grid points to draw each curve.

...

Other graphical arguments passed to plot.default.

Value

Invisibly, a list (one element per drawn fit) of data frames with the curve coordinates (fpr, tpr, and lb, ub when plot.ci = TRUE).

Examples

data(IVD)
fit1 <- reitsma.sroc(TP = TP, FN = FN, FP = FP, TN = TN, data = IVD)
plot(fit1, plot.ci = TRUE, spoint.region = TRUE)

plot(fit1, add.study = TRUE)                             # add the studies

plot(fit1, add.study = TRUE, study.size = "precision")   # point size by precision


if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## fit2 <- hattori.tsroc(...)       # see ?hattori.tsroc
plot(fit2)                          # one page per time point, <Return> for next
plot(fit2, time = 36)               # a single time point
plot(fit2, overlay = TRUE)          # all time points in one panel
} # }
